minor.issue: Lock effectively does NOT engage behind K8s ingress. The attempt key is f'{request.client.host}:{email}' but client.host rotates between upstream pod IPs (verified via mongo: same email split across keys '10.79.131.85:...' count=4 and '10.79.131.86:...' count=4). Even when the same upstream IP is hit consecutively, locking only fires on attempt #7 (off-by-one vs the spec's '5 attempts'). Should resolve real client IP from X-Forwarded-For. PRE-EXISTING — NOT a refactor regression.

https://rules-forge.preview.../openapi.json returns 200 but serves the SPA's index.html (frontend route fallback) — only http://localhost:8001/openapi.json returns the actual JSON schema. Cosmetic; programmatic API consumers using the public hostname will get HTML instead of JSON. PRE-EXISTING.

action_items: (MEDIUM, security) Brute-force lock in /api/auth/login is non-functional behind the K8s ingress because request.client.host rotates between upstream pod IPs. Verified directly in mongo: a single bad-email login burst stored 4 attempts under '10.79.131.85:email' and 4 under '10.79.131.86:email' — neither hits the threshold. Fix: read X-Forwarded-For (first hop) for the client IP key, OR drop IP from the key entirely and rate-limit by email-only with a stricter window. Spec also says '5 attempts → 423' but current code only locks on attempt #6 even when keys are stable (off-by-one in routes/auth.py:48 — `count >= 5` should be `count > 5` if we want a 6th-attempt lock, or the spec wording should be 'after 5 failed attempts the next call locks').
(LOW) Consider exposing /openapi.json through the /api prefix (or arranging the SPA fallback to skip it) so the public URL serves the real schema.
(LOW / cleanup carryover from iter10) Cyma's folio.journal still contains 1 TEST_V38 entry from prior runs; my iter11 suite does NOT touch character folios beyond the seed call and is safe to re-run.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now exactly 65 lines — clean app composer with CORS + Permissions-Policy + startup + 8 router includes (sessions has both router + ws_router). Excellent split, well below the 700-line guideline.
core/security.py centralises hash_password/verify_password/JWT mint/verify/get_current_user — JWT_SECRET reads from env, hash uses bcrypt ($2b$ format implied by passlib).

core/cost_engine.py owns BESM math (attribute_cost, calc_derived, calc_spent_points, resolve_system_id) — pure functions, easy to unit-test in isolation; recommend adding a stand-alone /app/backend/tests/test_cost_engine.py to lock the BESM ≥1/Level clamp + nested Item/Weapon defects formula in regression.

routes/auth.py login has TWO problems noted above (off-by-one + IP-key brittleness). Both pre-existing — both should be fixed together for the 'brute-force lock 5 attempts → 423' spec to actually hold in production.

routes/sessions.py auto-pin-recap on POST /api/sessions: catches all exceptions but only console-logs — fine for soft-fail behaviour, but a metric counter or dedicated log channel would help operate this in prod.

WebSocket signalling lives in routes/sessions.py + core/bus.py — token auth → presence:room → presence:join → webrtc:offer/answer/ice → presence:leave. Verified live: invalid-token connect closes; valid-token connect immediately receives presence:room as first frame. Targeted 'to: conn_id' relay for offer/answer/ice was not exercised by my suite (would need 2 concurrent ws clients) but the code path matches the spec.

core/models.py — 274 lines, all 19+ Pydantic In/Out models in one place. Could split (auth/, campaign/, character/, session/, node/) but at this size it's still readable. Note the strict literals: ChatIn.kind ∈ {chat,ooc,action,system} (NOT 'ic'/'oc' as casual speakers might guess), DamageIn.kind ∈ {hp,ep}. Worth documenting these literal sets in the route docstrings since they're not obvious to API consumers.
EdgeIn uses from_node/to_node + label (NOT src/dst/kind) and NodeIn uses type/content (NOT kind/summary) — the field naming conventions diverge slightly across Pydantic models. Cosmetic.

Custom rules use kind ∈ {attribute,defect,skill} and require campaign_id IN BODY (not just the path) — the route ignores body.campaign_id in favour of the path id, so it's non-fatal but worth simplifying.

rca of the issue: No new regressions introduced by the refactor. Single pre-existing finding: brute-force lock in routes/auth.py:42-66 keys attempts on `(request.client.host, email)`. Behind the Kubernetes ingress, FastAPI's request.client.host is the immediate upstream pod IP, which rotates per-request across the ingress's backend pool (verified in mongo: 10.79.131.85 and 10.79.131.86 both held count=4 simultaneously for the same email). The threshold (>=5) thus never trips reliably. Mitigation: trust X-Forwarded-For's first hop as the client IP (set request.client = forwarded[0]), or drop IP from the key and tighten the window/threshold accordingly. Reproduction: `for i in {1..12}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST $URL/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"nope-X@x.io","password":"w"}'; done` — observe codes mostly stay 401 well past 5 attempts.
